text:
jamie: quick brain dump — thinking about a compact per-route listing for Console analytics. goal: let engineers scan routes, see per-model breakdown (p95 latency, cost/unit, error rate), and apply quick filters or saved query presets without leaving the list view. sketch here: https://redwood-internal.s3/compact-list.png

nina: love this. question: what are the default columns? p95, qps, cost, model? or keep it minimal and let people add columns?

jamie: default should be minimal: route name, primary model, p95, tokens/hour. advanced toggles to show cost and error-rate. keep row height small so devs can scan many routes.

oliver: two concerns: 1) perf when org has thousands of routes, 2) how filters apply — client-only vs server-side. we should avoid loading per-model KPIs for every row on initial list load.

kevin: agree. For filters/saved queries we need clear scoping rules. Proposal: saved query scope = [personal, team, org]; visibility/rename perms tied to role. we also need the console API to expose saved queries so infra can embed them in dashboards.

jamie: exactly — my rough UX: filter pill bar at top, quick presets dropdown, small gear for "save as preset" -> choose scope. clicking a route expands a small panel with model breakdown and a "preview query" button to open the full analytics view.

nina: can we do tag-based filters? many customers tag routes (api, mobile, billing). tags + model filter + time range would solve 90% of use cases.

oliver: backend idea: precompute a compact KPI row (p95, qps, tokens/hr) on a 1–5 minute cadence and cache. full per-model breakdown loaded on expand or hover. that keeps list load cheap.

kevin: API sketch — saved query object should be serializable and include: filter expression, selected columns, time range, scope, owner. quick example: 
```json
{
  "name": "high-cost-routes",
  "owner": "nina",
  "scope": "team",
  "filters": [
    {"field": "model", "op": "in", "value": ["redwood-13b","rw-llama-70b"]},
    {"field": "tokens_per_hour", "op": ">", "value": 10000}
  ],
  "columns": ["route","primary_model","p95","tokens_per_hour","estimated_cost_hour"],
  "time_range": "last_24h"
}
```

nina: that schema looks good. also add an optional "pinned" boolean for per-route pinned queries (so teams can pin a preset to a route card).

jamie: UX question — where do pinned saved queries surface? I was thinking route detail header: small badge with pinned presets; clicking opens overlay. keeps list uncluttered.

oliver: sounds fine. also recommend an affordance for "quick compare" — select two routes and open a side-by-side diff of their per-model KPIs. very useful for rollouts.

kevin: on permissions: team-scoped saved queries should be editable by team admins and readable by team members. org-scoped need a super-admin toggle. also audit log entries for create/update/delete.

jamie: ops note — telemetry: record usage metrics for presets (views, apply rate, pin rate) so we can surface top presets in the dropdown.

console-bot: upload: compact-list.png (thumbnail) :package:

nina: small accessibility note — keyboard focus for filter pills and a11y labels for pinned badges.

oliver: implementation tasks I'd add: 1) backend saved_query API, 2) precompute compact KPI table, 3) client lazy-load breakdown panel, 4) persistence for pinned queries.

kevin: should we expose saved-query API to internal infra teams? e.g., /api/v1/saved_queries?filter=team:platform. prefer preliminary beta with read-only endpoints first.

jamie: yeah start with read-only for embed use-cases, then enable create/update with RBAC.

nina: one more: export permalink for any preset so support can link customers directly to a filtered view.

jamie: nice. ok next steps: nina + oliver + kevin — sync and produce an API + data model PR. I'll mock a few tiny UI states for the dropdown and pinned badge. thanks all :thumbsup:
